issues.description: Three concerns complected in one loop: readiness signaling, data accumulation, and EOF detection
issues.detail: The function mixes non-blocking polling, blocking drain, and process-exit checks in one tangled control flow. The hybrid mode-switch makes the time semantics ambiguous: 'when does this read complete?' now has two different answers depending on which branch you entered. Separate the readiness-wait from the drain-to-EOF. Two small functions, one concern each.

issues.description: Mutating the fd's O_NONBLOCK flag in place is place-oriented programming on a shared resource
issues.detail: fcntl flips a flag on the file descriptor and never restores it. The fd is an identity; its blocking-mode is a value that now changes mid-function with no record. If anything else holds or inherits this fd, its observed behavior silently changed. Either own the fd fully (open blocking from the start once you know you want it) or restore the flag in a finally.

issues.description: The real question wasn't asked: why is this an ad-hoc FIFO protocol instead of a framed stream
issues.detail: The bug is truncated JSON because the protocol has no length, no delimiter, no end marker — just 'read until the pipe closes and hope.' The fix patches the read side; it does not address that the value being transported (one JSON document) has no explicit boundary. A length prefix or newline-delimited framing makes EOF-detection a non-problem. Hammock first.

issues.description: Dead branches and a bare pass replace prior logic without explaining what changed semantically
issues.detail: The else and except BlockingIOError now both fall through to pass. The previous code carried real information (has_blocking_error, the MacOS comment, the check_process_exited fallback). Deleting it without stating which cases the new blocking-drain provably covers leaves future readers guessing what regressed and what didn't. Name the cases.

issues.description: check_process_exited is now only consulted on the 'no content ever arrived' path, silently narrowing its role
issues.detail: Previously it disambiguated 'process gone, pipe quiet' mid-stream. Now it only fires if zero bytes were ever read. That may be correct given the blocking drain, but the change in responsibility is implicit. State it: 'once first byte arrives, EOF is determined solely by blocking read returning 0.' Make the invariant visible in a comment or a named helper.

issues.description: No test pins the race the patch claims to fix
issues.detail: The PR asserts a POSIX guarantee resolves an intermittent race, but adds no test that exercises a slow writer, a fast-exiting writer, or a partially-buffered pipe. Tests don't make code simple, but they do pin the time semantics you're now relying on. Without one, the next refactor will reintroduce the truncation.

review.summary: The fix likely works, but it is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: a mode-flip on a live fd plus a nested drain loop, layered onto a protocol that never specified its own end. The real complecting is at the protocol layer — one JSON document is being sent over an unframed byte stream, so 'where does the value end?' is being answered by OS-level pipe semantics instead of by the data itself. The patch trades one race for tighter coupling to POSIX blocking-read behavior and a mutated fd flag that is never restored. Decompose: wait-for-ready, drain-to-EOF, and frame-the-payload are three separate concerns. The question that should have been asked first: why isn't the writer sending a length or a newline?
